dct_description_sm: The 1996  Census  Public  Use  Microdata  File  (PUMF)  on  Families contains data based on a 2.8% sample of the population enumerated in the census. It provides information on the demographic, social and economic characteristics of the census families and non-family persons. This microdata file allows users to group and manipulate the data to suit their own requirements.  Data replaced 17 January 2003  DATA ERRORS  Please be advised that errors have been detected with four variables and the resulting data on this CD-ROM product.    The two variables, FULL-TIME OR PART-TIME WEEKS WORKED IN 1995 BY THE MALE SPOUSE, MALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, MALE LONE PARENT OR MALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (FPTWKM) and FULL-TIME OR PART-TIME WEEKS WORKED IN 1995 BY THE FEMALE SPOUSE, FEMALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, FEMALE LONE PARENT OR FEMALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (FPTWKF), were found to contain unjustifiably high counts in their "Not applicable" categories. The source code used in the creation of the variables was examined and it was found to be in error. The logic used in the derivation of the variables lacked specificity and, as a result, families may have been erroneously classified according to the characteristics of a member to whom the concept did not apply.    Furthermore, the code for LEGAL MARITAL STATUS OF THE MALE COMMON-LAW  PARTNER, MALE LONE PARENT OR MALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (MARSTLM) and LEGAL MARITAL STATUS OF THE FEMALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, FEMALE LONE PARENT OR FEMALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (MARSTLF) incorrectly assigned a large number of units to the divorced category, and this thereby affected the quality of the remaining categories.  The discrepancies have now been corrected, and the present data for these variables has been verified to be correct. Also, all other variables have been completely re-verified and are correct on this CD-ROM product. No other problem variables were found on either the 1996 Census PUMF Households and Housing or Individuals Files.   In addition, the control counts for the above variables were updated in the 1996 PUMF Families File User Documentation.    DATA QUALITY INFORMATION INCONSISTENCIES   Inconsistencies were also identified with some of the data quality information found on all three 1996 Census PUMF files. After a thorough review of the data quality information, all errors relating to data quality information have now been corrected. The following is a list of the inconsistencies that were identified:   Errors were identified in the "Quality of Estimates" tables found on all three 1996 PUMF files. An incorrect formula was used for calculating the coefficient of variation in the case of quantitative variables (e.g. income) for these tables. The "Quality of Estimates" tables can be found in Chapter III (Sampling Method and Data Quality) of the 1996 PUMF User Documentation.    Since Example 4 in Chapter III uses results obtained from the "Quality of Estimates" tables, this example was also incorrect on all three files.   Further to the main error mentioned above, some inconsistencies were also identified between the English and French versions of the "Quality of Estimates" files.   In addition to the User Documentation, the following "Quality of Estimates" files were also affected by the problems noted above.     CENSUS FAMILY TYPE (CFTYPE) Explanatory Note  An explanatory note has been appended to the description of the CENSUS FAMILY TYPE (CFTYPE) variable in the 1996 Census PUMF Families File User Documentation. The appended note provides additional clarification regarding conceptual differences which can occur when the CFTYPE variable is cross-tabulated with the PRIMARY HOUSEHOLD MAINTAINER INDICATOR FOR THE MALE SPOUSE, MALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, MALE LONE PARENT OR MALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (HMAINM) or PRIMARY HOUSEHOLD MAINTAINER INDICATOR FOR THE FEMALE SPOUSE, FEMALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, FEMALE LONE PARENT OR FEMALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (HMAINF) variables in the 1996 PUMF Families File.   For further information, please refer to the description of the CFTYPE variable in the 1996 PUMF Families File User Documentation.      !-- IMPORTANT NOTE FROM STATISTICS CANADA 27 MARCH 2001  A university researcher recently called into question two variables found on the 1996 Family level Public Use Microdata File. The two variables, FULL-TIME OR PART-TIME WEEKS WORKED IN 1995 BY THE MALE SPOUSE, MALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, MALE LONE PARENT OR MALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (FPTWKM) and FULL-TIME OR PART-TIME WEEKS WORKED IN 1995 BY THE FEMALE SPOUSE, FEMALE COMMON-LAW PARTNER, FEMALE LONE PARENT OR FEMALE NON-FAMILY PERSON (FPTWKF), were felt to contain unjustifiably high counts in their not applicable categories.  Production and Subject Matter staff have examined the source code used in the creation of the variables and have found it to be in error. The logic used in the derivation of the variables lacked specificity and, as a result, families may have been erroneously classified according to the characteristics of a member to whom the concept did not apply.  While there is no evidence, at this time, that similar errors appear on either the Individual or Household files, the Census Dissemination Project Team has called for a complete review of all three files.  Until the results of this investigation are known,  existing users of the Families file should be cautioned not to use the problem variables and informed that they will receive a corrected file (via CD-ROM) in the near future. --     ISLAND data extraction available through Additional Files
